dedupe_keys.name: spatial accessibility trauma capable hospital supply and firearm violence in metropolitan rio de janeiro 2025

description: This data set brings together where shootings happened in Metropolitan Rio de Janeiro in 2025, where the hospitals able to treat trauma are, and how easily people in each area can reach them. The producer is Valdecy Pereira of the Universidade Federal Fluminense. Coverage is 21 municipalities of the metropolitan region, month by month in 2025. The GeoPackage combines geolocated firearm-violence records from the Crossfire (Fogo Cruzado) monitoring platform, census population from IBGE, monthly facility data from Brazil's National Registry of Health Establishments (CNES) and road travel times from OpenStreetMap; it holds a hexagonal grid with population and firearm burden, accessibility scores for hospital beds and adult intensive care beds computed with the enhanced two-step floating catchment method, and a layer of hospitals judged trauma-capable from their registered resources. The file is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with a data dictionary. Caveats: the producer states that trauma capability is potential structural capability, not formal certification or real-time readiness, and that accessibility is modelled, not observed ambulance travel. Simulation uses: matching trauma capacity to violence hotspots, and testing how hospital closures or road blockages affect access to emergency surgery. Related records: the Spanish hospital accessibility data (data-spain-hospital-accessibility-census-tracts) use a simpler nearest-hospital measure.
name: Spatial accessibility, trauma-capable hospital supply and firearm violence in Metropolitan Rio de Janeiro, 2025
schema_summary: GeoPackage layers: study-area municipalities (21), 2025 firearm events, hexagonal analysis grid with population and firearm burden, month-specific road-network travel times, E2SFCA accessibility to total hospital beds and adult ICU beds, and a CNES-derived trauma-capability hospital layer
